content.text:
You are a veteran Capcom NES pixel artist and art director for Mega Man 2-3. You are shown ONE small enemy sprite,
at 1x (true size, left) and enlarged with nearest-neighbour scaling (right), on a neutral grey-blue background
that is not part of the sprite.

The sprite is supposed to be this enemy:
"A small floating robot squid, Blooper-like, that swims along at and after Mega Man in pulses (tentacles gather, then thrust). It is a swimming mine: when it gets close its eyes flash red, then it explodes."
Intended size: about 16x16 to 20x20 px. Game: Mega Man 2-3 (NES).

Judge whether it is a convincing authentic NES Mega Man enemy that matches the description. Be calibrated:
authentic Capcom enemy sprites score about 90-95; competent fan art about 60-70; amateur or AI-looking pixel art
about 30-45. Do not reward or punish a sprite for being recognisable; judge what you see.

Criteria, 0-10 each:
- authenticity: could ship unchanged in MM2/MM3 (Capcom conventions, not "modern pixel art")
- description_fidelity: matches the description (body, features, role)
- readability_1x: the silhouette and features read instantly at true size
- pixel_craft: 1-px black outlines used the Capcom way, clean clusters, no jaggies, orphans, dithering or noise
- palette_discipline: NES colours, flat shading with at most one highlight, about 3 colours + transparent per 8x8 tile
- appeal: charm and character in the Capcom manner

Return ONLY a JSON object:
{"subscores": {"authenticity": n, "description_fidelity": n, "readability_1x": n, "pixel_craft": n,
  "palette_discipline": n, "appeal": n},
 "score": 0-100 overall,
 "verdict": "convincing" or "not_convincing",
 "issues": ["specific, located problems"],
 "fixes": ["specific pixel-level fixes"]}

message.content: {"subscores":{"authenticity":4,"description_fidelity":4,"readability_1x":6,"pixel_craft":6,"palette_discipline":4,"appeal":6},"score":50,"verdict":"not_convincing","issues":["At 1x the silhouette reads as a round fish with a pointed striped tail, not a squid with separate thrusting tentacles.","The long right-side appendage forms one rigid triangular mass; it does not suggest tentacles gathering and extending in pulses.","The face uses large rectangular eye sockets and broad interior bands, giving it a modern icon-like construction rather than an MM2/MM3 enemy face.","Black contour thickness is inconsistent around the lower body and tail joint, creating heavy black blocks instead of a controlled 1-pixel outline.","Several isolated blue and white steps along the tail produce a busy striped pattern that competes with the face.","The sprite appears to use black, white, cyan, medium blue, and dark blue within compact tile areas, exceeding the disciplined three-colour-plus-transparency look.","There is no visible mine or warning-state cue beyond the eyes; the current dark eyes do not establish a clear area for a red flash frame."],"fixes":["Replace the triangular tail with three or four individually separated 1-pixel-wide tentacle tips, leaving transparent gaps between them.","Orient the body vertically with a domed mantle above and short tentacles below or behind, so the squid silhouette reads at 1x.","Reduce the face to two compact eye clusters with one dark pupil pixel each; reserve those pupil pixels for red in the warning frame.","Use one dark outline colour, one main blue or cyan, and one light highlight colour per hardware sprite tile; remove one of the intermediate blues and most white striping.","Make the outer contour consistently one source pixel thick, especially beneath the body and where the tentacles attach.","Consolidate the interior shading into two or three larger clusters rather than horizontal bands and isolated stair-step pixels.","Create at least two animation frames: tentacles gathered close to the body, then tentacles extended backward for the thrust pulse."]}
